skill.name: bark-notify
skill.description: Send Bark push notifications when Codex or Claude tasks finish, including device, project, status, and a concise result summary.
skill.summary: Send structured Bark alerts when AI coding tasks finish.
skill.author: caopulan

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, shell line continuations, standard installation paths, and specific configuration variable reads. Two medium risks remain: dry-run output reveals the Bark key, and a custom endpoint receives that key plus task metadata. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Dry-run output exposes the Bark key inside the request URL.
remediation.suggestion: Redact the Bark key before printing the request URL, or omit the URL entirely.

remediation.issue: A configurable endpoint receives the Bark key and task details.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS and reject unexpected schemes or untrusted hosts before sending credentials and task details.

semantic_findings.title: Dry-Run Output Exposes Bark Key
semantic_findings.description: Dry-run mode prints the complete request URL after placing the Bark key in its path, exposing the credential to terminals and logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The URL directly includes parse.quote(bark_key), and dry-run mode prints that URL without redaction.

semantic_findings.description: A custom CODEX_BARK_BASE_URL receives the Bark key, machine name, project, status, and summary, enabling leakage if configuration is untrusted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The environment controls the destination, while the request URL carries the Bark key and the payload contains task context.

content.user_title: Send Bark Notifications After AI Tasks
content.value_statement: Long-running AI tasks can finish without drawing attention. This skill sends a Bark push with device, project, status, and summary details.
actual_capabilities: Sends Bark notifications through an HTTP POST request.
Includes device, project, status, and result summary in each notification.
Accepts task title, status, summary, project name, and timeout options.
Resolves project names from AGENTS.md or the current folder.
Supports dry-run previews and configurable Bark endpoints.
limitations: Requires Python 3, network access, and a working Bark service.
Requires manually configured machine name and Bark key environment variables.
Sends notification content to the configured endpoint without automatic secret redaction.
Reports supplied status text and does not independently verify task success.

use_cases.title: Monitor Long Coding Tasks
use_cases.description: Receive a mobile alert when a local Codex or Claude coding task finishes.

use_cases.title: Track Automated Maintenance
use_cases.description: Send concise completion status after repository checks, migrations, or documentation updates.

use_cases.title: Follow Remote Workflows
use_cases.description: Receive project and status details while working away from the development machine.

best_practices: Keep task summaries concise and remove credentials, customer data, and private source content.
Use a trusted HTTPS Bark endpoint and protect the key environment variable.
Keep dry-run output private because the current helper prints the Bark request URL.
anti_patterns: Do not place secrets or complete command output in notification summaries.
Do not send notifications to an endpoint that you do not control or trust.
Do not treat a notification status as independent proof that a task succeeded.

faq.question: What configuration is required?
faq.answer: Set CODEX_MACHINE_NAME and CODEX_BARK_KEY. CODEX_BARK_BASE_URL is optional and defaults to the Bark API.

faq.question: How is the project name selected?
faq.answer: The helper uses an explicit argument, then AGENTS.md metadata, then the current project folder name.

faq.question: Can I use a self-hosted Bark server?
faq.answer: Yes. Set CODEX_BARK_BASE_URL to a trusted HTTPS endpoint that you control.

faq.question: What data leaves my machine?
faq.answer: The configured endpoint receives the Bark key, task title, machine name, project name, status, and summary.

faq.question: Can I test without sending a notification?
faq.answer: Yes. Dry-run mode previews the request, but its current output includes the Bark key in the URL.

faq.question: Which status values are supported?
faq.answer: The helper accepts any text. Common values include success, failed, partial, and blocked.
